SERVING
SIZE:
3 medium, raw (150 g)
able year-round, but the peak season for
fresh figs lasts from June to October.
Uses
Fresh figs should be plump and fairly soft
but free of bruises. Figs are quite perish-
able and should be refrigerated no more
than 7 days.  Delicious as a snack, figs
also can be diced and added to salads and
other dishes or used for pie fillings and
preserves.  Figs also add sweetness and
moisture to baked goods.
Nutrient composition
Raw figs are a good source of vitamin B6and
are high in dietary fiber.  (See the Appendix,
page 434, for the nutrient content of dried
figs.)
The fig is a pleasantly sweet fruit that consists of a soft flesh pursed around a large
number of tiny edible seeds.  It can be eaten whole, peeled or unpeeled.  Under
certain circumstances, the natural sugars crystallize on the surface of the fruit,
making the fruit sweeter.
